option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。grows herbs and salad greens at Alvarez Farm 表示他是種植者；answers shoppers' questions there about choosing and storing produce 表示他在市集為顧客提供建議。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。公告最後署名的是 Joan Whitfield, Market Manager。Ruben Alvarez 在公告中以第三人稱被提及（Mr. Alvarez will keep a notebook），並不是張貼公告的經理。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。寫短箋給市集的是顧客 Margaret Lindqvist（Shopper Margaret Lindqvist sent us this note）。Ruben Alvarez 是她在短箋中提到、她去請教問題的對象。

evidence.quote: Ruben Alvarez, who grows herbs and salad greens at Alvarez Farm, answers shoppers' questions there about choosing and storing produce
Our May newsletter included an article by volunteer writer Colette Dubois
Shopper Margaret Lindqvist sent us this note
Joan Whitfield, Market Manager

explanation.takeaway_zh: 人物身分題常把文中其他人的角色放進選項作為干擾。先圈出每個人名，再找名字前後的頭銜、關係子句或文末署名，把「人名—角色」逐一配對，最後才比對經過改寫的選項。

questions.prompt: What is suggested about Ms. Lindqvist's opinion of the Fresh Advice table?

options.label: A
options.text: She doubts that its storage tips work at home.

options.label: B
options.text: She considers it mainly suitable for experienced cooks.

options.label: C
options.text: She appreciates the practical advice she has received there.

options.label: D
options.text: She would rather read written answers than ask questions in person.

explanation.summary_zh: Lindqvist 照著建議保存羅勒後效果良好，之後每週六都帶著新問題回來，還帶了剛開始用新鮮香草做菜的鄰居同行。由此可推知她肯定諮詢桌提供的實用建議，答案是 C。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 她在短箋中沒有直接說 helpful 或 appreciate，但描述了具體結果和後續行動：(1) 她依 Mr. Alvarez 的建議，把羅勒放在廚房流理台上的一杯水裡，結果 stayed fresh for a full week，表示這次建議對她有效；(2) I have returned every Saturday since with a new question，表示她持續使用這項服務；(3) 她帶了剛開始用新鮮香草做菜的鄰居一起去，表示她願意把這項服務分享給別人。綜合這幾句，可以推論她對諮詢桌提供的實用建議抱持正面、肯定的態度。其他選項則是文中找不到支持，或與她描述的結果不符。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。文中沒有任何她懷疑建議的表述；而且她在自家廚房流理台（the kitchen counter）照著建議做，羅勒保存了整整一週，她描述的結果顯示這個方法在她家中有效，因此 A 不成立。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。文中只說鄰居剛開始使用新鮮香草做菜，不能據此判定她整體的烹飪經驗。Lindqvist 帶鄰居前往並持續請教，顯示她願意使用和分享服務；文中沒有支持她認為服務「主要適合有經驗的廚師」，因此 B 缺乏根據。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。建議帶來具體效果（羅勒保鮮一週），加上她之後每週六回來提問並帶鄰居同行，這些行為都支持她肯定諮詢桌提供的實用建議。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。問答筆記本是經理宣布的未來安排（Mr. Alvarez will keep a notebook...），不是 Lindqvist 提出的要求。她雖多次當面詢問，但文中沒有比較她對書面與口頭解答的偏好，因此無法支持 would rather read written answers。

evidence.quote: He suggested keeping it in a glass of water on the kitchen counter instead, and my last bunch stayed fresh for a full week.
I have returned every Saturday since with a new question.
Last week I brought along my neighbor, who has just started cooking with fresh herbs.
Mr. Alvarez will keep a notebook of common questions and answers at the table starting this Saturday

explanation.takeaway_zh: 推論態度題中，說話者不一定會直接使用 helpful、disappointed 等評價字眼。可以從「採納建議後的具體結果」以及「之後的行動」（例如再訪、帶人同行）來判斷態度。排除選項時，要分清「文中沒有根據」與「與文意矛盾」；也要確認選項中的細節（例如筆記本）是由誰提出的，避免把別人的安排誤當成說話者的意見。

content.title: Updated Review of a Coworking Space
content.scenario_summary: A founder posts an updated review of Harbor Loft Coworking on a review site. The previous spring she gave it three stars because its private offices were too small for the workbenches her team used to assemble smart water meters. In January, utility customers told her that clear data reports mattered more than new meters. Her company stopped making devices and now designs online dashboards on laptops. The shared desks, phone booths and meeting rooms now suit the team. The front desk moved the team to shared-desk memberships within a week and waived the change fee. She raises her rating from three to five stars and recommends the space to founders who are unsure of their future needs. The first question contrasts the explicitly addressed readership with people who are only mentioned. The second separates the review's purpose, revising an outdated rating, from the business change that explains the revision and from incidental praise.

blocks.text: DeskFinder Reviews: Harbor Loft Coworking
Reviewer: Marisol Vega, founder of Tidewell Studio
Rating: 5 of 5 (previously 3)
Posted: March 12

Last spring I gave Harbor Loft three stars. Its private offices were too small for the workbenches my team needed to assemble smart water meters, and I said so. I'm updating my rating because that complaint no longer reflects how we work.

In January, two of our utility customers told us that clear reports on their water data mattered more to them than new meters. We stopped making devices and now design online dashboards instead. That work happens entirely on laptops, and the shared desks, quiet phone booths and bookable meeting rooms suit it far better than any workshop would. Harbor Loft's front-desk team also moved us from our private office to four shared-desk memberships within a week and waived the usual change fee.
My recommendation is for founders who can't yet be sure what their company will need six months from now. Harbor Loft gives you room to change course.

questions.prompt: For whom is Ms. Vega's review mainly intended?

options.label: A
options.text: Utility companies seeking clearer reports on their water data

options.label: B
options.text: Teams looking for space to assemble electronic devices

options.label: C
options.text: Harbor Loft staff who handle membership changes

options.label: D
options.text: Founders who are uncertain about their companies' future needs

explanation.summary_zh: 評論最後一段明確指出，這份推薦是寫給「還無法確定公司六個月後需要什麼的創業者」，所以答案是 D。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 判斷讀者時，可以先找文中直接點名對象的句子。最後一段寫 "My recommendation is for founders who can't yet be sure what their company will need six months from now."，接著用 you 對這群人說 "Harbor Loft gives you room to change course."。選項 D 的 uncertain about their companies' future needs，就是 can't yet be sure what their company will need 的換句話說。其他選項中的人物（公用事業客戶、組裝裝置的團隊、櫃台人員）在內容裡都有出現，但他們是被描述的對象，評論並沒有把建議寫給他們。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 文中的公用事業客戶是 Ms. Vega 公司的客戶。他們告訴她，清楚的數據報告比新水錶重要，接著她的公司就轉型了。他們是故事中的角色，不是這篇評論要提供建議的讀者。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 需要工作台組裝智慧水錶的是 Ms. Vega 自己的團隊，而且是過去的情況，也是她去年春天只給三星的原因。評論沒有向正在找組裝空間的團隊提出任何建議。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 櫃台團隊協助轉換會員方案並免收變更手續費，但文中是以第三人稱描述他們。評論中的 you 承接前一句的 founders，"Harbor Loft gives you room to change course" 這句是對創業者說的，不是對空間員工說的。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。"My recommendation is for founders who can't yet be sure what their company will need six months from now" 直接點出讀者，選項是這句話的同義改寫。

evidence.quote: My recommendation is for founders who can't yet be sure what their company will need six months from now.
Harbor Loft gives you room to change course.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 問讀者對象時，先找 "My recommendation is for..."、"If you are..." 這類直接點名的句子，並確認 you 指的是誰。文中提到的客戶或員工，不一定就是文章的讀者。

questions.prompt: Why did Ms. Vega post the review?

options.label: A
options.text: To announce that her company now designs online dashboards

options.label: B
options.text: To revise a rating she gave the space the previous year

options.label: C
options.text: To ask Harbor Loft to offer larger private offices

options.label: D
options.text: To thank the staff for waiving a membership change fee

explanation.summary_zh: Ms. Vega 明說她要更新去年春天給的三星評分，因為當時的抱怨已不符合公司現在的工作方式。評分欄也顯示從 3 星改為 5 星，所以答案是 B。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 目的題要分清「發文要做什麼」和「為什麼這樣做」。第一段先交代去年春天給了三星，接著說 "I'm updating my rating because that complaint no longer reflects how we work."，評分欄也寫著 "5 of 5 (previously 3)"，可見發文的目的是修改舊評分。第二段的轉型經過（不再製造裝置、改做線上儀表板）正是她修改評分的原因，說明舊抱怨為何不再成立。櫃台協助換方案、免收手續費，則是支持較高新評分的補充優點。所以轉型和免收費用都是解釋評分改變的內容，發文的目的是更新評分，而不是宣布公司的新業務或感謝員工。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公司改為設計線上儀表板確實是她修改評分的原因。不過她提到這件事，是為了解釋舊抱怨為何不再適用，評論的重點是對 Harbor Loft 的評價，不是向讀者宣布公司的新業務。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。"Last spring I gave Harbor Loft three stars" 交代了先前的評分，"I'm updating my rating..." 說明這次發文要更新評分，評分欄的 "previously 3" 也證實她改了先前的評價。發文日期是 March 12，可合理推得 last spring 指的是前一年的春天，也就是選項中的 the previous year。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 私人辦公室太小是她去年春天的抱怨。她現在明說那個抱怨已不符合團隊的工作方式，團隊也已從私人辦公室改用共用座位，文中沒有要求提供更大的辦公室。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 櫃台一週內完成方案轉換並免收平常的變更手續費，是以 also 帶出的補充優點，用來支持較高的新評分。文中沒有表示她是為了感謝員工而發文。

evidence.quote: Last spring I gave Harbor Loft three stars.
I'm updating my rating because that complaint no longer reflects how we work.
Rating: 5 of 5 (previously 3)
We stopped making devices and now design online dashboards instead.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 作答目的題時，先找說明發文動作的句子。如果主要子句已經有具體動作（如本文的 I'm updating my rating），because 後面通常是在解釋這個動作的原因，屬於支持內容；但如果主要動詞只是籠統的 I'm writing，目的可能就在 because 子句中（例如 I'm writing because I'd like to request a refund）。最後仍要以作者想透過這篇文字達成什麼來判斷。

content.title: Credit for a Narrow-Gate Delivery
content.scenario_summary: In an event-equipment rental company's delivery team chat, a coordinator thanks a senior driver for moving an evening reception's heater delivery from a box truck to a van because the venue gate is too narrow. He corrects her: a newer colleague measured the gate during a Tuesday site visit and changed the vehicle on the work order. The newer colleague says he checked the route only because the senior driver sent him while the senior driver went through the heater layout with the client. He adds that the senior driver made him go back when he forgot to check for low branches. The newer colleague is driving again today while the senior driver rides along and fills out forms. The senior driver also has the colleague deal with the venue staff himself this time and will step in only if needed. The coordinator notes that the colleague's own van will be ready on Monday, so the shared ride is temporary. She confirms the departure time, gate unlocking time, heater deadline and guest arrival time, and she plans to credit the newer colleague in the team notes. The first question requires two complementary cues to infer that the senior driver is helping his colleague prepare to drive without him. The first cue is that the senior driver corrects the colleague's route check and entrusts him with the venue contact while riding along. The second cue is that the shared-van arrangement ends on Monday. One distractor claims the ride-along continues after Monday. The second question tests the meaning of a correction about who made a decision, with a lure based on another meaning of 'call'. The third asks for the gate unlocking time among the departure, deadline and guest arrival times.

documents.title: Corliss Event Rentals Delivery Team Chat

blocks.text: Corliss Event Rentals: Delivery Team Chat

The Harbor Arts Council just called to confirm tonight's reception at Maple Court. Hugo, great call moving their heaters from the box truck to the van. The truck would never have fit through the Alder Lane gate.
blocks.speaker: Lena Varga

blocks.text: That wasn't my call, actually. Sam measured the gate when we stopped by on Tuesday and changed the vehicle on the work order. It's barely seven feet wide.
blocks.speaker: Hugo Delgado

blocks.text: Only because Hugo sent me to check the route from the street while he went through the heater layout with the arts council. When I forgot to check for low branches, he made me go back.
blocks.speaker: Sam Whitfield

blocks.text: Either way, it saved us a second trip. Are you two still leaving at 2:30?
blocks.speaker: Lena Varga

blocks.text: Yes. Sam's driving again today, and I'll just ride along and fill out the setup forms. Sam, you're dealing with the venue staff yourself this time. I'll only jump in if you need me.
blocks.speaker: Hugo Delgado

blocks.text: Sam, your own van will be ready on Monday, so enjoy the company while it lasts.
blocks.speaker: Lena Varga

blocks.text: Ha! I will.
blocks.speaker: Sam Whitfield

blocks.text: Also, the venue will unlock the gate at 3:00. The heaters need to be running by 5:30, and guests arrive at 6:00.
blocks.speaker: Lena Varga

blocks.text: Got it. I'll let the venue know when we're ten minutes away.
blocks.speaker: Sam Whitfield

blocks.text: Thanks, both of you. Sam, I'm adding your gate check to Friday's team notes.
blocks.speaker: Lena Varga

questions.prompt: What is most likely true about Mr. Delgado?

options.label: A
options.text: He will keep riding along with Mr. Whitfield after Monday.

options.label: B
options.text: He is learning the job from a more experienced coworker.

options.label: C
options.text: He is helping a coworker prepare to drive without him.

options.label: D
options.text: He will be given his own van on Monday.

explanation.summary_zh: Sam 漏查低垂樹枝時，Hugo 要他回去補查；今天 Hugo 又讓 Sam 自己與場地人員接洽，只在需要時才介入。Lena 則指出 Sam 星期一就會有自己的車，同車只是暫時的。結合這兩組線索，最合理的推論是：Hugo 正在幫 Sam 為不再與他同車出勤做準備。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 文中沒有人直接說明兩人的關係，必須結合兩組線索。第一組線索顯示指導的方向。Sam 說他忘了檢查低垂的樹枝時，Hugo 要他回去補查，這是在糾正他的疏漏。今天由 Sam 開車、Hugo 隨車，而 Hugo 說這次由 Sam 自己與場地人員打交道，他只在需要時介入；「this time」暗示這項接洽工作這次才交給 Sam 處理。這些行動顯示 Hugo 在糾正 Sam，並逐步放手讓他自己處理，不只是兩位同事單純分工。不過只看這組線索，看不出這樣安排的目的。第二組線索是時間範圍。Lena 說 Sam 自己的車星期一就會準備好，並說「enjoy the company while it lasts」，表示兩人同車只是暫時的。只看這句，只能知道共乘即將結束，無法判斷誰在指導誰。兩組結合後可以推知：在 Sam 開始開自己的車、不再有 Hugo 同車之前，Hugo 一面糾正他，一面把任務交給他獨立處理，最可能是在幫他準備獨自出勤。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。此選項指的是星期一之後 Hugo 仍繼續隨車。Lena 說 Sam 自己的車星期一就會準備好，同車作伴只到「while it lasts」為止，表示這段共乘是暫時安排。文中沒有任何內容顯示 Sam 有了自己的車之後，Hugo 還會繼續隨車。今天 2:30 兩人同行出發，是星期一之前的安排，不能用來支持此選項。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤，關係方向相反。Sam 漏查樹枝時，是 Hugo 要他回去補查；把與場地人員接洽的工作交給 Sam、自己只在需要時介入的，也是 Hugo。文中沒有任何內容顯示 Hugo 在向較有經驗的同事學習。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。Hugo 糾正 Sam 漏查樹枝，又讓 Sam 自己接洽場地人員、只在必要時介入，顯示他在指導 Sam，並逐步交付任務。Lena 說 Sam 星期一起就有自己的車，同車只是暫時的。兩者結合，可推斷 Hugo 是在 Sam 開始獨自開車前陪同他，幫他做準備。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。Lena 這則訊息開頭稱呼「Sam」，星期一會拿到自己的車的是 Sam，不是 Hugo。此選項把 Sam 的安排套到 Hugo 身上。

evidence.quote: When I forgot to check for low branches, he made me go back.
Sam's driving again today, and I'll just ride along and fill out the setup forms. Sam, you're dealing with the venue staff yourself this time. I'll only jump in if you need me.
Sam, your own van will be ready on Monday, so enjoy the company while it lasts.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 推論人物關係時，要找出能分辨關係方向與目的的具體行動，例如誰糾正誰的疏漏、誰把新任務交給誰處理，再搭配這項安排是否有期限。單看分工或共乘本身，無法區分指導關係與一般合作。

questions.prompt: At 1:04 P.M., what does Mr. Delgado most likely mean when he writes, "That wasn't my call, actually"?

options.label: A
options.text: Someone else decided to switch to the van.

options.label: B
options.text: He did not take the arts council's phone call.

options.label: C
options.text: He thinks switching to the van was a mistake.

options.label: D
options.text: He was not there when the gate was measured.

explanation.summary_zh: Lena 稱讚 Hugo 把暖爐改由廂型車載運是「great call」（好決定）。Hugo 回答「That wasn't my call, actually」，意思是這個決定不是他做的。他接著說明是 Sam 量了大門寬度並修改工作單，藉此更正 Lena 對功勞歸屬的誤會。
explanation.reasoning_zh: Hugo 的 call 承接 Lena 前一則訊息中的 great call，在這裡指「決定、判斷」；句尾的 actually 帶有更正對方說法的語氣。Hugo 隨即說明，Sam 在星期二兩人前往時量了門寬，並在工作單上更改車輛，可見做出改車決定的是 Sam。他還補充大門勉強才七英尺寬，表示他認同這個決定，並不是在撇清一個錯誤決定的責任。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。Lena 以為改車是 Hugo 的決定，Hugo 否認後立刻說明是 Sam 量了大門並在工作單上更改車輛，所以他的意思是決定是由別人（Sam）做的。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。Lena 第一句的 called 確實是指藝術協會打來的電話，但她接著用 great call 稱讚改車的決定。Hugo 的回覆也都在談量門寬與改車，與接電話無關。此選項把這裡的 call 誤解為「電話」。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。That wasn't my call 有時可用來撇清某個不好決定的責任，但 Hugo 接著說大門「barely seven feet wide」，呼應 Lena 所說卡車根本進不去，顯示他認為改用廂型車是對的。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。「when we stopped by on Tuesday」只顯示 Hugo 參與了星期二的到訪；Sam 後來也提到，當時 Hugo 正在和藝術協會討論暖爐配置，所以文中無法確定 Hugo 是否在量門現場。不論如何，Hugo 這句話否認的是改車的決定出自他，並不是在談自己是否在場，所以 D 不是這句話的意思。

evidence.quote: The Harbor Arts Council just called to confirm tonight's reception at Maple Court. Hugo, great call moving their heaters from the box truck to the van.
That wasn't my call, actually. Sam measured the gate when we stopped by on Tuesday and changed the vehicle on the work order. It's barely seven feet wide.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 意圖題要把引句放回對話中理解：先找出對方原本的說法（這裡是 Lena 把功勞歸給 Hugo），再看說話者接下來如何補充，才能判斷多義字（如 call）在此的意思與說話目的。

questions.prompt: When is the gate at Maple Court scheduled to be unlocked?

explanation.summary_zh: Lena 說場地方面會在 3:00 打開大門的鎖，因此大門預定在下午 3:00 開鎖。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 題目問大門何時開鎖，對應的是 Lena 所說的「the venue will unlock the gate at 3:00」。聊天中的其他時間各屬不同事項：2:30 是 Lena 詢問、Hugo 回答 Yes 所確認的出發時間；「The heaters need to be running by 5:30」是指到 5:30 時暖爐必須已在運轉，可以更早，by 表示不晚於該時間，包含該時點；這是暖爐運轉的期限，不是開門時間。6:00 則是賓客抵達的時間。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。2:30 是 Lena 問「Are you two still leaving at 2:30?」、Hugo 回答 Yes 所確認的出發時間，不是大門開鎖的時間。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。Lena 明確表示場地方面會在 3:00 打開大門的鎖。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。Lena 說「The heaters need to be running by 5:30」，意思是到 5:30 時暖爐必須已在運轉，可以更早；by 表示不晚於該時間，包含該時點。這是暖爐必須運轉的期限，與大門開鎖時間無關。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。6:00 是賓客抵達的時間（guests arrive at 6:00），不是大門開鎖的時間。

evidence.quote: Also, the venue will unlock the gate at 3:00. The heaters need to be running by 5:30, and guests arrive at 6:00.
Are you two still leaving at 2:30?

explanation.takeaway_zh: 時間細節題要先鎖定題目所問的事件（開門），再找文中對應的動詞（unlock）及其時間。文中其他時間分別屬於出發、暖爐運轉期限與賓客抵達，不要張冠李戴。by 5:30 指到 5:30 時暖爐必須已在運轉，可以更早；by 表示不晚於該時間，包含該時點。

content.title: Handing Over a Home Testing Panel
content.scenario_summary: A customer insights manager at a fictional kitchen-appliance maker e-mails an employee who is taking over the company's home testing panel from a colleague who is transferring to another office. The panel's 40 households each try a prototype appliance for two weeks and then join follow-up video calls. The e-mail sets out her new duties: shipping prototypes, arranging and scheduling the calls the colleague has led, and sending monthly summaries. It notes that the product team will still choose which prototypes go out. It also says that the colleague will share a household spreadsheet the following week. Finally, it suggests that she join his final call only as a listener and notes that panel members praise his relaxed questioning style. The questions test the inferred motive for this suggestion, a NOT-mentioned duty (prototype selection, which stays with another team), and the duration sense of 'runs'.

documents.title: E-mail: Taking over the home testing panel

blocks.text: From: Gareth Moyo <g.moyo@pellhamkitchen.example>
To: Lena Ortiz <l.ortiz@pellhamkitchen.example>
Date: March 3
Subject: Taking over the home testing panel
Hi Lena,
Thank you for agreeing to take over our home testing panel from Adrian Kwok, who moves to our Brisbane office at the end of March. From April 1, the panel will be entirely yours.

The 40 households on the panel each try a prototype appliance for two weeks. You will ship the prototypes to them and arrange the follow-up video calls, which Adrian has led since the panel began. Each call runs about thirty minutes, but please schedule them at least an hour apart so you can write up your notes. You will also send the product team a monthly summary of the households' comments. As before, that team will decide which prototypes go out and when.

Adrian keeps a spreadsheet of each household's address and preferred call times, and he will share it with you next week. His final follow-up call before the move is with the Hartley household on March 21. Panel members often say his relaxed way of asking questions makes them comfortable giving honest opinions. I suggest that you join that call, but only as a listener; you won't need to say anything.

Best regards,
Gareth Moyo
Customer Insights Manager

questions.prompt: Why most likely does Mr. Moyo suggest that Ms. Ortiz join the call on March 21?

options.label: A
options.text: To introduce herself to the Hartleys as their new contact

options.label: B
options.text: To receive the household spreadsheet from Mr. Kwok

options.label: C
options.text: To learn which prototype the Hartleys will test next

options.label: D
options.text: To observe Mr. Kwok's way of interviewing households

explanation.summary_zh: Ms. Ortiz 即將接手 Adrian 一直主持的後續視訊訪談。3 月 21 日那通是 Adrian 調職前的最後一次訪談，受訪家庭也常稱讚他輕鬆的提問方式。Mr. Moyo 請她「只以旁聽者身分」參加，由此可推知，用意是讓她觀摩 Adrian 如何訪談這些家庭。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 信中沒有直接說出建議旁聽的理由，要把兩組線索連起來。(1) 第二段說，她負責安排的後續視訊訪談一直由 Adrian 主持；第一段又說四月起整個小組都交給她。可見這些訪談今後將由她接手。(2) 第三段指出，3 月 21 日是 Adrian 調職前的最後一通訪談；受訪者表示，他的提問方式讓他們願意說出真實意見；而 Ortiz 只需旁聽。即將接手的人以旁聽身分參加前任者的最後一次訪談，信中又特別點出前任者的提問風格受到好評。因此最有根據的推論是：讓她觀察 Adrian 的訪談方式。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中建議她 only as a listener，也就是只旁聽、不擔任發言角色。若目的是向 Hartley 家自我介紹、成為新的聯絡人，她就得在通話中開口，與這項安排不符。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中確實提到 Adrian 保存一份試算表，記錄各家庭的地址與偏好通話時間。不過信中另外說明他會在 next week 分享給她，並沒有把取得試算表當作參加 3 月 21 日訪談的理由。這個選項把試算表的安排錯接到旁聽建議上。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中寫明 that team will decide which prototypes go out and when，決定寄出哪些原型、何時寄出的是產品團隊。信中也沒有把這通訪談和 Hartley 家下一個要測試的原型連在一起，此選項缺乏根據。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。一方面，她將接手 Adrian 主持的訪談；另一方面，這是 Adrian 的最後一次訪談，他的提問方式受到好評，而她只需旁聽。兩者結合，可推得用意是觀摩他訪談家庭的方式。

evidence.quote: From April 1, the panel will be entirely yours.
arrange the follow-up video calls, which Adrian has led since the panel began

His final follow-up call before the move is with the Hartley household on March 21. Panel members often say his relaxed way of asking questions makes them comfortable giving honest opinions. I suggest that you join that call, but only as a listener; you won't need to say anything.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 推論動機時可以分兩步。先確認當事人即將承擔什麼工作，再看這項安排有什麼特點（例如「最後一次」「只旁聽」「方式受好評」），兩者的交集通常就是作者的用意。若選項和原文的安排相衝突，或把信中另一件事錯接過來，就應該排除。

questions.prompt: What is NOT mentioned as one of Ms. Ortiz's new responsibilities?

options.label: A
options.text: Sending prototype appliances to panel members

options.label: B
options.text: Selecting the prototypes that households try

explanation.summary_zh: 信中說 As before, that team will decide which prototypes go out and when，其中 that team 指前一句的 product team。決定寄出哪些原型仍由產品團隊負責，並沒有交給 Ortiz，所以 B 不是她的新職責。
explanation.reasoning_zh: NOT 題要逐一核對：三個選項在信中有對應敘述，剩下一個則沒有提到或與原文相反。第二段交代她要做的事有三項：把原型寄給家庭、安排並排定後續視訊訪談、每月向產品團隊提交意見摘要。同段最後一句的 that team 承接前一句的 the product team，As before 表示選定原型的工作沿用以往分工。要注意，「寄送原型」與「決定寄出哪些原型」處理的是同一批物品，但負責的人不同。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中說 You will ship the prototypes to them，them 指小組的家庭。把原型寄給小組成員是她的新職責，有提到。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確答案。信中說 that team will decide which prototypes go out and when，負責選定原型的是產品團隊，不是 Ortiz，因此不屬於她的新職責。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中說她要 arrange the follow-up video calls，並請她 schedule them at least an hour apart。為各家庭排定視訊訪談時間是她的工作，有提到。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 信中說 You will also send the product team a monthly summary of the households' comments。每月把家庭的意見彙整後回報，有提到。

evidence.quote: You will ship the prototypes to them and arrange the follow-up video calls
please schedule them at least an hour apart
You will also send the product team a monthly summary of the households' comments.
As before, that team will decide which prototypes go out and when.

explanation.takeaway_zh: NOT 題有時會把同一物件的不同動作分給不同的人（例如寄送與選定）。作答時要同時核對「做什麼」和「由誰做」，並留意 that team 這類指涉詞指的是誰，不要一看到相同的名詞就認定有提到。

questions.prompt: In the e-mail, the word "runs" is closest in meaning to

explanation.summary_zh: Each call runs about thirty minutes 中，runs 後面接一段時間長度，表示每通訪談「持續」約三十分鐘，與 lasts 同義。
explanation.reasoning_zh: run 是多義動詞，要看主詞和後面接的成分來判斷字義。這裡主詞是 call（通話），後面接 about thirty minutes（時間長度）。後半句請她把通話間隔至少一小時，好有時間寫筆記，可見這句談的正是通話持續多久。把 lasts 代入成 Each call lasts about thirty minutes，意思不變，結構也相同：動詞不接受詞，後面直接接時間長度。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: manages 對應 run 作「經營、管理」的意思，此時後面接被管理的對象，如 run a business。代入成 Each call manages about thirty minutes，句子無法成義，因為通話並不是在管理三十分鐘。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: operates 對應 run 表示機器或服務「運轉、營運」的用法，如 The shuttle runs on weekdays。這裡要表達的是一通電話持續多久，代入成 Each call operates about thirty minutes 無法表達這個時間長度。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。lasts 表示持續一段時間，代入後與原句意思和結構都一致，也符合後半句要預留時間寫筆記的安排。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: flows 對應 run 表示液體流動的用法，如 water runs down the window，與通話的時間長度無關。

evidence.quote: Each call runs about thirty minutes, but please schedule them at least an hour apart so you can write up your notes.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 多義字代換題的作法：先看主詞是什麼，再看後面接的是受詞、時間長度還是地點。接著把每個選項代回原句，確認意思與語法角色都維持不變。

content.title: Harbor Cruise Support Chat
content.scenario_summary: In a customer-support chat, a passenger says a harbor cruise's tour page promised thirty minutes ashore at a lighthouse, but her boat only circled the island. The agent explains that the harbor authority closed the island dock on May 6 after an inspector found damage, so tours now go through a shipyard channel instead. She booked on May 3. Closure notices have appeared on the tour page and in booking confirmation e-mails only since May 7. She asks for a full refund for two tickets. The agent tactfully declines by citing the rule for company-cancelled sailings and offers to refund the landing fee included in each ticket instead. She accepts. The questions test a polite refusal, a stated reason distinguished from its outcome, and a chronology inference about what her confirmation e-mail could not have contained.

documents.title: Customer support chat with Saltmarsh Harbor Cruises

blocks.text: Saltmarsh Harbor Cruises — Customer Support Chat
Date: May 9

Hello. My husband and I took the 2:00 P.M. Lighthouse Loop yesterday. Your tour page promised thirty minutes ashore at Pellam Point Lighthouse, but our boat only circled the island before heading through the old shipyard.
blocks.speaker: Keiko Tanaka

blocks.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Tanaka. On May 6, an inspector found damage to the Pellam Point dock, and the harbor authority closed it that day. Until it reopens, our captains can't land passengers there, so they've been taking guests through the shipyard channel instead.
blocks.speaker: Rafael Ibarra

blocks.text: The shipyard was pleasant enough, but the lighthouse visit was the whole reason I booked this tour on May 3. And nobody mentioned the closure when we checked in.
blocks.speaker: Keiko Tanaka

blocks.text: You should have been told at check-in, and I'll raise that with our check-in team. Since May 7, a closure notice has also appeared on the tour page and in the confirmation e-mail we send at the moment of booking.
blocks.speaker: Rafael Ibarra

blocks.text: Either way, I'd like a full refund for both tickets.
blocks.speaker: Keiko Tanaka

blocks.text: I understand. Full refunds are reserved for sailings we cancel before departure, I'm afraid. What I can do is return the $12 landing fee included in each ticket.
blocks.speaker: Rafael Ibarra

blocks.text: All right. Please return the fees to the card I paid with.
blocks.speaker: Keiko Tanaka

blocks.text: Done. Both fees should reach that card within five business days.
blocks.speaker: Rafael Ibarra

questions.prompt: At 9:49 A.M., what does Mr. Ibarra most likely mean when he writes, "Full refunds are reserved for sailings we cancel before departure, I'm afraid"?

options.label: A
options.text: Her tour will be treated as a cancelled sailing.

options.label: B
options.text: She should have cancelled her booking before departure.

options.label: C
options.text: He cannot refund the full price of her tickets.

options.label: D
options.text: Her request needs approval from the check-in team.

questions.target_text: Full refunds are reserved for sailings we cancel before departure, I'm afraid

explanation.summary_zh: Tanaka 女士在 9:47 要求兩張票全額退款。Ibarra 先生回覆全額退款只適用於公司在出航前取消的航班，接著又提出退還登島費的替代方案，可見他是在婉拒全額退款。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 意圖題要把引句放回對話脈絡理解。她先提出 I'd like a full refund for both tickets。他沒有直接說 no，而是說明全額退款的適用條件：由 we（Saltmarsh 公司）在出航前取消的航班。她在 9:41 說明夫妻倆昨天搭了這趟船，船也繞島航行，可見這班船並未被取消，不符合這個條件。I'm afraid 用來委婉帶出壞消息，後面的 What I can do is... 改提較小的補償，也證實前一句是在拒絕她的要求。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。他說明的是全額退款適用的情況，而她搭的航班已照常出航。他並沒有把她的行程當成取消航班處理，所以只提出退還每張票內含的 12 美元登島費。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。sailings we cancel 中的 we 指 Saltmarsh 公司，before departure 是公司取消航班的時間點，並不是說乘客應該自己在開船前取消訂位。對話中也沒有提到乘客取消訂位的規定。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。引句陳述的退款條件把她已出航的航班排除在外，接著 What I can do is return the $12 landing fee 改提較小的補償，表示他無法退還票價全額。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。check-in team 出現在 9:46，他是要向報到團隊反映報到時沒人告知碼頭關閉一事。退還登島費由他本人處理，9:51 直接回覆 Done.，沒有提到需要報到團隊核准。

evidence.quote: My husband and I took the 2:00 P.M. Lighthouse Loop yesterday.
I'd like a full refund for both tickets.
Full refunds are reserved for sailings we cancel before departure, I'm afraid. What I can do is return the $12 landing fee included in each ticket.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 客服婉拒時常不直接說 no，而是「說明適用條件＋I'm afraid＋What I can do is...」。解題時先找出對方提出的要求，再判斷說話者陳述的條件是否把這個要求排除在外，並留意後面是否改提替代方案。

questions.prompt: According to Mr. Ibarra, why are the tours not stopping at Pellam Point?

options.label: A
options.text: Harbor officials have shut the Pellam Point dock.

options.label: B
options.text: An inspector found damage to the tour boats.

options.label: C
options.text: The route now passes through the shipyard channel.

options.label: D
options.text: The lighthouse building is closed for repairs.

explanation.summary_zh: Ibarra 先生說港務局在 5 月 6 日關閉了 Pellam Point 的碼頭。碼頭重新開放前，船長無法讓乘客在那裡上岸，所以行程不在那裡停靠。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 題目問的是原因。9:43 的訊息形成一條因果鏈：檢查人員發現碼頭受損 → 港務局當天關閉碼頭 → 碼頭重新開放前，船長無法讓乘客在那裡上岸。接在 so 後面的 they've been taking guests through the shipyard channel instead 是無法上岸後的替代安排，屬於結果。選項 A 以 Harbor officials have shut 改寫 the harbor authority closed it。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。the harbor authority closed it that day 中的 it 指 the Pellam Point dock。碼頭關閉後，在重新開放前船長無法讓乘客上岸。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。檢查人員發現的損壞在 Pellam Point 的碼頭（dock），不是遊船。這個選項把損壞套到了錯誤的對象。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。改走船廠水道寫在 so 之後，是無法上岸後採取的替代路線，屬於結果而不是原因。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。對話中被關閉、等待重新開放的是碼頭，並沒有提到燈塔建築關閉或整修。

evidence.quote: On May 6, an inspector found damage to the Pellam Point dock, and the harbor authority closed it that day. Until it reopens, our captains can't land passengers there, so they've been taking guests through the shipyard channel instead.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 原因題要沿著句中的連接詞判斷因果方向。本題 so 前面的「碼頭關閉、無法上岸」是原因，so 後面的「改走船廠水道」是結果。同時也要確認原因中的對象是否正確，例如受損的是碼頭還是船。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the confirmation e-mail that Ms. Tanaka received?

options.label: A
options.text: It was sent on May 7 together with a closure notice.

options.label: B
options.text: It did not mention the closure of the dock.

options.label: C
options.text: It described the shipyard channel as a new stop.

options.label: D
options.text: It offered to refund the landing fee.

explanation.summary_zh: 確認信在訂位當下寄出，而她是 5 月 3 日訂位，所以她的確認信在 5 月 3 日寄出，早於 5 月 6 日的碼頭關閉，因此信中不會提到碼頭關閉。關閉通知從 5 月 7 日起才加入確認信，也與這個推論一致。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 先排出時間線：5 月 3 日她訂位，同時收到確認信 → 5 月 6 日檢查人員發現碼頭受損，港務局當天關閉碼頭 → 5 月 7 日起確認信開始附上關閉通知 → 之後她才搭船。對話沒有直接說出她的確認信內容，但結合「確認信在訂位當下寄出、她 5 月 3 日訂位」與「碼頭 5 月 6 日才關閉」即可推出：信寄出時碼頭尚未關閉，自然不會提到此事。關閉通知 5 月 7 日起才加入確認信，則進一步佐證這一點。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。5 月 7 日是關閉通知開始出現在行程頁面和確認信的日期。確認信在訂位當下寄出，她 5 月 3 日訂位，所以她的確認信不是 5 月 7 日寄出的。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。她的確認信在 5 月 3 日訂位時寄出，早於 5 月 6 日的碼頭關閉，因此信中不會提到碼頭關閉；關閉通知 5 月 7 日起才開始加入確認信，也佐證這一點。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。改走船廠水道是 5 月 6 日碼頭關閉後才開始的安排。她的確認信寄出時這件事尚未發生，信中不可能把船廠水道寫成新的停靠點。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯誤。退還 12 美元登島費是 Ibarra 先生在這次對話中回應她的退款要求時才提出的補償。對話中沒有任何資訊顯示確認信曾提供這項退款。

evidence.quote: the lighthouse visit was the whole reason I booked this tour on May 3
On May 6, an inspector found damage to the Pellam Point dock, and the harbor authority closed it that day.
Since May 7, a closure notice has also appeared on the tour page and in the confirmation e-mail we send at the moment of booking.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 遇到多個日期時，把「文件何時產生」與「事件何時發生」排成一條時間線，就能判斷某份文件當時可能或不可能包含哪些資訊。

blueprint.event: a difference between a promise and an experience

content.title: Brightwater Call Coach Program
content.scenario_summary: An insurance claims center's learning team writes to advisors who passed the Level 2 assessment at the end of their first year. This milestone qualifies them to coach, and from October they will guide new advisors. Each coaching shift follows five steps: collecting a call plan from the training coordinator, who pairs advisors with coaches and chooses the call types to practice; a listen-in hour; a role switch with feedback notes; a shift record whose new coach sign-off column (the inserted sentence) responds to trainee confusion found in last spring's pilot; and a ten-minute replay of a call chosen by the trainee. Pilot supervisor Marcus Lee's review found that trainees who replayed a call with their coach were no faster at handling calls in their second week but made far fewer errors, so the replay became a required step. Because it adds time, some coaches asked to skip it on busy days, but he wants it kept on every shift, even the busiest. The questions test the coordinator's duty against a close rival (the trainee's choice of replay call), problem-to-fix sentence insertion, the supervisor's unstated attitude toward the replay, and the main instructional purpose. The supervisor question's key is that Lee values the reduction in trainee errors more than the time the replay adds; the passage never states this weighing. His review identifies the benefit as fewer errors rather than speed, which rules out the rival that he expects the replay to save time later by making trainees faster. His insistence on keeping the time-consuming replay on every shift, even the busiest, shows how he weighs that benefit against its cost and rules out the rival that he would let coaches skip it when call volume is high. The remaining distractor misreads the 'no faster' result as doubt about the replay's usefulness, which the required-step decision and his response contradict. The purpose question sets the instructional purpose against a true announcement of the October coaching role and a true explanation of why the replay became required.

blocks.text: Brightwater Insurance Claims Center: Call Coach Program
From: Learning and Development Team
To: Advisors who passed the Level 2 assessment in September

Congratulations on passing the Level 2 assessment at the end of your first year. [[1]] Only advisors who have reached this level may coach others, and from October you will guide new advisors through their first month on the phones. Each coaching shift follows five steps.

Step 1: Before the shift, pick up your trainee's call plan from Dina Rocha. As training coordinator, she matches each new advisor with a coach and decides which types of calls the trainee should practice.
Step 2: For the first hour, let your trainee listen in on your calls. [[2]] Explain what you did after each caller hangs up, not during the conversation.
Step 3: Then switch places so that your trainee handles calls while you listen. Note one strength and one area to improve for each call.

Step 4: Keep the shift record up to date. During last spring's pilot, several trainees were unsure which tasks their coach had already checked. [[3]] Initial each task in that column as soon as your trainee completes it correctly.
Step 5: Spend the last ten minutes replaying a recorded call with your trainee, who chooses which call to review.

The pilot was run by claims supervisor Marcus Lee. His review found that trainees who replayed a call with their coach were no faster at handling calls in their second week than those who did not, but they made far fewer errors. [[4]] As a result, the replay has been made a required step. Because it adds time, some coaches have asked to skip it when call volume is high. Mr. Lee, however, wants it kept on every shift, even the busiest.

questions.prompt: What is one of Dina Rocha's responsibilities?

options.label: A
options.text: Selecting which recorded call is replayed

options.label: B
options.text: Initialing completed tasks on the shift record

options.label: C
options.text: Reviewing the results of last spring's pilot

options.label: D
options.text: Selecting the kinds of calls trainees practice

explanation.summary_zh: Step 1 說明訓練協調員 Dina Rocha 負責兩件事：替每位新進客服人員配對指導員，以及決定學員該練習哪些類型的來電。D「挑選學員練習的來電類型」改寫了後者。
explanation.reasoning_zh:
Step 1 第二句的 she 指前一句的 Dina Rocha，As training coordinator 說明她的職稱。原文 decides which types of calls the trainee should practice 對應 D 的 Selecting the kinds of calls trainees practice。其他選項的動作在文中都有出現，但執行者不是 Dina：
- 決定回放哪通錄音的是學員。
- 在紀錄欄位簽上姓名縮寫的是本文讀者，也就是即將擔任指導員的人。
- 試辦由 Marcus Lee 主持，評估試辦結果的也是他（His review）。

A 和 D 都與「選擇通話」有關。作答時要分清兩點：選的是練習的來電類型，還是回放的那一通錄音；以及由誰來選。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。Step 5 的 your trainee, who chooses which call to review 中，who 修飾 your trainee，所以決定回放哪一通錄音的是學員。Dina 決定的是學員要練習的來電「類型」，不是回放用的那一通錄音。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。Initial each task in that column 是對讀者（即將擔任指導員的人）的指示，要他們在學員正確完成任務後簽上姓名縮寫。Step 4 沒有提到 Dina 負責輪班紀錄。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。試辦由理賠主管 Marcus Lee 主持，下一句 His review found... 的 His 也指他，所以評估試辦結果的是 Mr. Lee。文中描述 Dina 職責的部分沒有提到試辦或其評估。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 對。decides which types of calls the trainee should practice 即「決定學員該練習哪些類型的來電」，與選項意思一致。

evidence.quote: Step 1: Before the shift, pick up your trainee's call plan from Dina Rocha.
As training coordinator, she matches each new advisor with a coach and decides which types of calls the trainee should practice.
Step 5: Spend the last ten minutes replaying a recorded call with your trainee, who chooses which call to review.
Initial each task in that column as soon as your trainee completes it correctly.
The pilot was run by claims supervisor Marcus Lee.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 人物職責題要同時確認「動作」和「執行者」。選項動詞相近時，先比較受詞的差別，再利用 she、who、his 等代名詞判斷動作由誰執行。

questions.prompt: Where would this sentence fit most naturally in the passage? "To address this, we have added a coach's sign-off column to the record."
questions.target_text: To address this, we have added a coach's sign-off column to the record.

explanation.summary_zh: 插入句說明，為了處理某個問題，紀錄中新增了指導員簽核欄。[3] 的前一句正好是問題：試辦期間有些學員不確定指導員已確認過哪些任務。Step 4 開頭也已提到 the shift record。後一句要求在 that column 簽上姓名縮寫，正好接續新增的欄位，因此答案是 [3]（C）。
explanation.reasoning_zh:
插入句有三個線索：
1. To address this 的 this 應指前文一個需要處理的問題。
2. 本題中，the record 可自然回指 Step 4 已提到的 the shift record，與新增簽核欄的主題一致；定冠詞本身不要求名詞一定先在前文明示。
3. 新增的 sign-off column 應與後文的說明接得上。

Step 4 先提到 the shift record，接著說試辦期間有些學員不確定指導員已確認過哪些任務，這是問題。插入句說明因此新增簽核欄，這是因應措施。後句要求指導員在 that column 簽上姓名縮寫，說明新欄位的用法。若沒有插入句，Step 4 前文沒有提到任何欄位，that column 便找不到明確指涉的欄位。

其他位置的問題如下：
- [1]、[2] 之前沒有待解決的問題，this 找不到合適的對象；簽核欄也會出現在與輪班紀錄無關的段落，與前後句的內容接不上。
- [4] 之前，Step 4 雖然較早提過輪班紀錄與學員的困惑，但 [4] 的前一句是回放的評估結果。插入句放在這裡，會夾在評估結果與 As a result 之間，打斷原本的因果銜接；Step 4 的 that column 也仍缺少先出現的欄位。

因此，[3] 同時具備明確的問題、已提到的 shift record，以及後句 that column 的承接，形成最連貫的「問題→因應措施→使用方式」順序。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。[1] 的前一句是恭賀讀者通過 Level 2 評鑑，不是需要 address 的問題，To address this 的 this 找不到合適的問題可指。此時文中也尚未談到任何紀錄，放在這裡，讀者不清楚 the record 指的是哪份紀錄。簽核欄還會出現在說明指導員資格的開頭段落，離真正使用它的 Step 4 很遠。後句談的是只有達到此等級的人才能擔任指導員，也與簽核欄無關。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。[2] 之前依序是恭賀與資格說明、Step 1 領取通話計畫，以及前一句請讀者讓學員旁聽通話，都不是需要 address 的問題，this 沒有合適的問題可指。前文只提過 call plan，尚未談到輪班紀錄，the record 在此沒有明確的對應對象。此外，簽核欄會在描述旁聽的 Step 2 中出現，與使用它的 Step 4 不在同一處。後句談的是何時向學員講解自己的做法，也與簽核欄無關。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 對。前一句「試辦期間有些學員不確定指導員已確認過哪些任務」就是 this 所指的問題，Step 4 開頭的 the shift record 是 the record 自然的對應對象。插入句新增的簽核欄接著成為後句 that column 所指的欄位，形成「問題→因應措施→使用方式」的順序。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。[4] 之前，Step 4 確實較早提過 the shift record 以及學員不確定任務是否已確認的問題，但中間隔了 Step 5 與試辦說明。[4] 的前一句是評估結果：做回放的學員第二週處理來電雖然沒有比較快，但錯誤明顯較少。放在這裡，this 最自然會被理解為這項評估結果，而它不是需要新增簽核欄來處理的問題。插入句也會夾在評估結果與 As a result, the replay has been made a required step 之間，打斷「評估結果→回放改為必要步驟」的因果銜接。此外，Step 4 的 that column 出現時，前文仍沒有提到任何欄位。

evidence.quote: Step 4: Keep the shift record up to date.
During last spring's pilot, several trainees were unsure which tasks their coach had already checked. [[3]] Initial each task in that column as soon as your trainee completes it correctly.
Congratulations on passing the Level 2 assessment at the end of your first year. [[1]] Only advisors who have reached this level may coach others
Step 2: For the first hour, let your trainee listen in on your calls. [[2]] Explain what you did after each caller hangs up, not during the conversation.
but they made far fewer errors. [[4]] As a result, the replay has been made a required step.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 插入句以 To address this 開頭時，先在前文找出待解決的問題（本題就在前一句）。本題也可利用 the record 與 Step 4 的 the shift record 的對應，並以前句的問題及後句 that column 的承接共同判斷位置。最後檢查插入後會不會打斷 As a result 等連接詞原本的因果關係。

questions.prompt: What does Marcus Lee most likely believe about the replay?

options.label: A
options.text: He values the reduction in trainee errors more than the time the replay adds.

options.label: B
options.text: He expects the replay to save time later by making trainees handle calls faster.

options.label: C
options.text: He would let coaches skip the replay on shifts with high call volume.

options.label: D
options.text: He doubts the replay is useful because it did not make trainees faster.

explanation.summary_zh: Marcus Lee 的評估發現，做回放的學員第二週處理來電並沒有比較快，但錯誤明顯較少。之後有些指導員以回放會增加時間為由，要求在通話量大時省略，他仍希望連最忙的班都保留。由「效益在於減少錯誤」加上「面對時間成本仍希望每班保留」，可推知他認為減少學員錯誤比回放多花的時間更重要（A）。文中沒有直接說出這項權衡。
explanation.reasoning_zh:
這題考的是文中沒有明說的權衡，需要把兩處線索接起來。
1. 評估結果（他看到的效益）：His review found that... no faster... but they made far fewer errors。回放的效益在於錯誤減少，評估沒有發現第二週處理速度上的效益。
2. 後續回應（他如何面對成本）：指導員要求省略的理由是 Because it adds time，也就是回放的時間成本。however 表示他的看法與這項要求相反，even the busiest 表示連最忙的班也不例外。

合起來看：他知道回放要多花時間，也知道它沒有讓學員處理得更快，仍希望每一班都做，可見他判斷減少錯誤比這段時間更重要。

兩處線索分別排除不同的選項：
- 只看回應，可知他希望保留回放，但看不出他重視什麼；B「回放能讓學員變快、日後省時」也能解釋他為何不在意多花時間。評估結果指出學員並沒有變快、效益是錯誤減少，B 才失去依據。
- 只看評估，可知回放能減少錯誤，但無法確定在通話量大的班次是否仍值得多花時間，C「通話量大時可省略」看似合理的折衷。他的回應表示希望連最忙的班都保留，才排除 C。
- D 把「沒有比較快」讀成否定回放，但同一句以 but 指出錯誤明顯較少，他也希望每班保留，都與「懷疑回放有用」相反。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 對。評估顯示回放的效益是學員錯誤明顯較少。面對以「增加時間」為由的省略要求，他仍希望每一班、包括最忙的班都保留回放。兩者合起來，可推知他把減少錯誤看得比回放所花的時間更重要。這項權衡文中沒有直接寫出，是由評估加上回應推得的。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。他的評估發現，做回放的學員第二週處理來電並沒有比沒做的人快，文中也沒有其他資料顯示回放日後能提升速度。他看到的效益是錯誤較少，「期待回放讓學員變快、日後省時」是過度延伸評估結果的推測。若只看他希望每班保留，B 似乎也說得通，所以需要靠評估結果排除。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。「通話量大時省略」正是部分指導員提出的要求，但 Mr. Lee, however, wants it kept on every shift, even the busiest 表示他並不贊成這個例外。若沒有這句回應，單憑評估結果和指導員的要求，無法判斷他是否會讓步。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。「沒有比較快」只是評估結果的一半，同一句接著以 but 指出做回放的學員錯誤明顯較少，文件也說回放因此成為必要步驟。他還希望連最忙的班都保留回放，與「懷疑回放有用」相反。

evidence.quote: The pilot was run by claims supervisor Marcus Lee.
His review found that trainees who replayed a call with their coach were no faster at handling calls in their second week than those who did not, but they made far fewer errors.
As a result, the replay has been made a required step.
Because it adds time, some coaches have asked to skip it when call volume is high. Mr. Lee, however, wants it kept on every shift, even the busiest.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 態度推論題要把「當事人看到的具體結果」和「他面對成本或反對時的回應」接起來：結果說明他重視的效益是什麼，回應說明他願意為這項效益承擔多少成本。常見陷阱有兩種：一是過度延伸結果，把「沒有變快」讀成「日後會變快」或「沒有用」；二是忽略回應，以為他會接受折衷。

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the document?

options.label: A
options.text: To inform advisors that they will begin coaching in October

options.label: B
options.text: To describe how advisors should run their coaching shifts

options.label: C
options.text: To explain why the replay is now a required step

options.label: D
options.text: To reply to coaches who asked to skip the replay on busy days

explanation.summary_zh: 這份文件寄給九月通過 Level 2 評鑑的客服人員。開頭說明他們從十月起將指導新進人員，並以 Each coaching shift follows five steps. 引出後文。Step 1 到 Step 5 逐一指示指導員在每個帶訓班次該做什麼，因此主要目的是說明如何進行帶訓班次（B）。
explanation.reasoning_zh:
主旨題要比較各選項涵蓋的範圍。

A 和 C 都是文中真實的內容。A 對應開頭段落中十月起開始指導新人的說明；C 對應最後一段：評估發現做回放的學員第二週雖然沒有比較快，但錯誤明顯較少，因此回放成為必要步驟。不過，開頭段落隨即以 Each coaching shift follows five steps. 轉入步驟說明，十月開始帶人只是使用這些步驟的背景；最後一段也只在解釋 Step 5 為何是必要步驟。

B 涵蓋 Step 1 到 Step 5 的全部指示。這些祈使句直接告訴讀者每個班次要做什麼，構成文件的主體；Step 4 的試辦說明與最後一段都在支持其中的步驟。

D 則把文中轉述的對象當成收件人。要求省略回放的 some coaches 只以第三人稱被提及，收件人是剛通過評鑑的客服人員。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯，但具迷惑性。開頭段落確實恭賀讀者通過 Level 2 評鑑，並說明從十月起他們將指導新進人員度過第一個月，這是真實的次要目的。不過這段隨即以 Each coaching shift follows five steps. 引出步驟說明，文件其餘部分都在交代每個班次的做法；十月開始帶人是這些指示的背景。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 對。Step 1 到 Step 5 依序指示讀者：領取學員的通話計畫、讓學員旁聽、交換角色並記下每通電話的優點與待改進之處、更新輪班紀錄、最後回放錄音，涵蓋帶訓班次從開始到結束的流程。開頭的角色說明和最後的試辦評估，都在為這套做法提供背景與理由。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯，但具迷惑性。最後一段確實說明，評估發現做回放的學員雖然沒有比較快，但錯誤明顯較少，因此回放成為必要步驟。但這只解釋 Step 5 一個步驟的由來，不涉及其他步驟的做法，屬於支持性的說明，不是整份文件的主要功能。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 錯。文件的收件人是九月通過 Level 2 評鑑的客服人員，要求在通話量大時省略回放的 some coaches 只以第三人稱被提及。文件轉述他們的要求，以及 Mr. Lee 希望每班保留回放的立場，並不是寫給這些指導員的回覆。

evidence.quote: To: Advisors who passed the Level 2 assessment in September
Congratulations on passing the Level 2 assessment at the end of your first year.
Only advisors who have reached this level may coach others, and from October you will guide new advisors through their first month on the phones. Each coaching shift follows five steps.
Step 1: Before the shift, pick up your trainee's call plan from Dina Rocha.
Step 5: Spend the last ten minutes replaying a recorded call with your trainee, who chooses which call to review.
but they made far fewer errors. [[4]] As a result, the replay has been made a required step.
Because it adds time, some coaches have asked to skip it when call volume is high. Mr. Lee, however, wants it kept on every shift, even the busiest.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 主旨題要分辨「貫穿全文的主要功能」和「真實但只支撐局部的內容」。先看收件人，以及開頭如何轉入正文，再看文件大部分在要求讀者做什麼。祝賀、角色說明或某個步驟的由來即使屬實，若只是背景或理由，就不是主要目的。

content.title: Community Garden Article: A First-Time Grower's Half Plot
content.scenario_summary: A local newspaper article profiles a community garden's new half-plot rental program for first-time growers through one renter, Grace Adeyemi. She had not applied for a standard plot because it seemed too much for a beginner with a full-time job to maintain. She was paired with a long-time member, Walter Osei, and expected him to give her a planting chart and rules. Instead, he asked what she liked to cook and how many evenings she could spare, and her answers shaped a small, manageable planting. Ruth Calder, who has kept a standard plot since 2012, sat out the program's first season because she doubted that beginners would stick with it. All ten first-season renters are returning, so the program is doubling to twenty half plots. Applications are invited from first-time growers and from experienced members willing to partner with them, and Calder submitted hers the day applications opened. The questions test the article's purpose (program expansion versus incidental details), a paraphrased reason for not renting a standard plot, and the insertion of an expectation-contrast sentence before an evaluation. They also test inferring Calder's unstated role this year by combining clues. Her long-time standard plot rules out renting a half plot, and sitting out the first season rules out having been a partner last year. Her application rules out staying out of the program, leaving only that she has offered to partner with a newcomer.

blocks.text: Starting Small at Larkspur Street
By Imogen Faraday, Halvern Courier, February 10

When Grace Adeyemi moved into an apartment on Delancey Road two years ago, she hoped to start growing her own vegetables. The apartment's only outdoor space, however, is a shady balcony. [[1]] The Larkspur Street Community Garden is a five-minute walk away, but its standard plots seemed far more than a beginner with a full-time job could keep weeded and watered, so she did not apply for one. Last spring, the garden began renting half plots to first-time growers, and Adeyemi was among the first ten to sign up.

The half plots cost $35 a season, half the standard fee, and include use of the garden's shared tools and rain barrels. Each newcomer is also paired with an experienced member. Ruth Calder, who has kept a standard plot since 2012, sat out that first season, doubting that beginners would stick with it. Adeyemi's partner was Walter Osei, who has gardened at Larkspur Street for eleven years. [[2]]

Adeyemi admits she expected Osei to hand her a planting chart and a list of rules at their first meeting. [[3]] She calls that conversation the most useful part of the program, because her answers decided what went into her half plot. They left out the melons she had hoped to try and chose lettuce, herbs and bush beans, all of which she could tend in two short visits a week. [[4]] "I grew less than I had planned," she says, "but I ate everything I grew."

With all ten first-season renters returning, the garden is doubling the program to twenty half plots. Applications from first-time growers and from experienced members willing to partner with them are due March 15 at larkspurgarden.example. Calder submitted hers the day applications opened.

questions.prompt: Why was the article written?

options.label: A
options.text: To announce a lower fee for the garden's standard plots

options.label: B
options.text: To profile a program for new gardeners that is expanding

options.label: C
options.text: To honor a long-time member for his years at the garden

options.label: D
options.text: To recommend vegetables that need little regular care

explanation.summary_zh: 文章以 Adeyemi 的經驗為例，介紹社區菜園去年春天開始的新手半塊菜地方案。最後一段報導方案將從十塊加倍為二十塊，並公布申請方式與截止日。因此，寫作目的是介紹一個正在擴大的新手方案。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 判斷文章目的時，要看全文主軸和促成報導的新消息。第一段說明菜園去年春天開始把半塊菜地租給第一次種菜的人。第二、三段介紹方案內容，包括費用、共用工具與雨水桶、搭檔制度，並透過一位租用者的經驗呈現成效。最後一段帶出新消息：第一季十位租用者全數續租，方案加倍為二十塊，開放第一次種菜的人與願意擔任搭檔的資深會員申請，截止日是 March 15。個人經驗是介紹方案的例子；費用、會員年資和作物種類都是附帶細節。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 文中提到半塊菜地每季 35 美元，是標準費用的一半。這只是說明半塊菜地的價格，文中沒有說標準菜地要降價。此選項把費用細節誤當成主旨。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。全文介紹專為新手設計的半塊菜地方案，結尾報導方案從十塊擴大為二十塊並開放申請，與「介紹一個正在擴大的新手方案」相符。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 選項的 his 指男性會員，文中符合的只有 Walter Osei。他在菜園種了十一年，但這只是介紹 Adeyemi 的搭檔時提供的背景。文章沒有表揚他，也不是為他而寫。另一位資深會員 Calder 的年資，也只是用來交代她和方案的關係。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 生菜、香草和四季豆是 Adeyemi 依自己的時間與飲食習慣選出的作物，屬於個人經驗中的細節。文章沒有向讀者推薦哪些蔬菜比較好照顧。

evidence.quote: Last spring, the garden began renting half plots to first-time growers
With all ten first-season renters returning, the garden is doubling the program to twenty half plots.
Applications from first-time growers and from experienced members willing to partner with them are due March 15 at larkspurgarden.example.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 作答報導文章的目的題時，要分清促成報導的新消息（例如方案擴大、開放申請）和用來舉例的個人故事或背景細節。只抓住某個細節的選項，通常不是主旨。

questions.prompt: Why did Ms. Adeyemi decide against renting a standard plot?

options.label: A
options.text: She doubted she could take care of a plot that large.

options.label: B
options.text: She thought the garden was too far from her apartment.

options.label: C
options.text: She considered the fee for a standard plot too high.

options.label: D
options.text: She planned to grow vegetables on her balcony instead.

explanation.summary_zh: 第一段指出，對一位有全職工作的新手來說，標準菜地似乎遠超過她能維持除草、澆水的範圍，所以她沒有申請。A 以「懷疑自己照顧不了那麼大的菜地」改寫了這個原因。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 關鍵句是 its standard plots seemed far more than a beginner with a full-time job could keep weeded and watered, so she did not apply for one。so 前面的部分就是她不申請的原因。選項把 keep weeded and watered（保持除草、澆水）改寫為 take care of，把 seemed far more than ... could 改寫為 doubted she could。距離、費用和陽台都是附近出現的事實，但文中沒有把它們當作她不申請的原因。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。文中說標準菜地看起來遠超過她這個新手能照顧的範圍，所以沒有申請，與「懷疑自己照顧不了那麼大的菜地」意思相同。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 文中明確說菜園離她家只要步行五分鐘（a five-minute walk away），與「太遠」相反。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 費用出現在第二段，只用來說明半塊菜地是標準費用的一半。文中沒有說她覺得標準費用太貴，也沒有把費用當作她不申請的理由。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 文中說公寓唯一的戶外空間是陰暗的陽台，並用 however 表示這不符合她想種菜的期望。文章沒有說她打算改在陽台種菜。

evidence.quote: its standard plots seemed far more than a beginner with a full-time job could keep weeded and watered, so she did not apply for one
The Larkspur Street Community Garden is a five-minute walk away
half the standard fee

explanation.takeaway_zh: 細節題常把附近出現的距離、費用等真實資訊放進錯誤選項。作答時，先找出與題目所問原因直接相連的句子（例如本題 so 前面的內容），再比對選項的改寫。

questions.prompt: Where would this sentence fit most naturally in the passage? "Instead, Osei began by asking what she liked to cook and how many evenings a week she could realistically spend at the garden."
questions.target_text: Instead, Osei began by asking what she liked to cook and how many evenings a week she could realistically spend at the garden.

explanation.summary_zh: 插入句以 Instead 推翻前句的預期：她原以為 Osei 第一次見面會給她種植表和規則清單，實際上他卻先問她問題。後句提到 that conversation 和 her answers，表示前面要先交代提問。因此插入句放在 [3]，能同時承接前句的預期並引出後句的評價。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 放在 [3] 時，文意依序是：先寫預期（拿到種植表和規則），再寫實際情況（Osei 問她喜歡煮什麼、每週實際能來幾個晚上），最後是評價（她認為那次談話是方案中最有用的部分，因為她的回答決定了菜地種什麼）。後面的「每週兩次短暫造訪」呼應「每週能來幾個晚上」，生菜、香草等作物則呼應「喜歡煮什麼」。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 位置 [1] 的前後文還在說明她公寓只有陰暗陽台、菜園就在附近但她沒申請標準菜地。這時她還沒參加方案，也還沒和搭檔見面；插入第一次見面時的提問，會跳到之後才發生的事，打斷前後脈絡。Instead 前面也沒有可以推翻的預期。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 位置 [2] 的前句只介紹 Osei 的資歷（在菜園種了十一年），沒有任何預期或原本做法可讓 Instead 推翻。她預期拿到種植表和規則，要到下一段開頭才出現；放在 [2] 會變成先寫實際情況、後寫被推翻的預期，順序顛倒。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。前句交代她的預期，插入句以 Instead 說明實際發生的事；後句再對那次談話和她的回答作出評價，前後銜接完整。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 位置 [4] 的前文已說兩人選定作物，而且她每週可以照顧兩次；插入句描述的卻是第一次見面一開始的提問，放在這裡時間順序倒置。對談話的評價也會出現在交代談話內容之前。

evidence.quote: Adeyemi admits she expected Osei to hand her a planting chart and a list of rules at their first meeting.
She calls that conversation the most useful part of the program, because her answers decided what went into her half plot.
Adeyemi's partner was Walter Osei, who has gardened at Larkspur Street for eleven years.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 遇到含對比詞（如 Instead）的插入句，先找前文中被推翻的預期或原本做法，再檢查後文是否接續插入句的內容（如 that conversation、her answers）。只看人名剛出現的位置，容易選錯。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Ruth Calder?

options.label: A
options.text: She has applied to rent one of the new half plots.

options.label: B
options.text: She was paired with a newcomer during last season.

options.label: C
options.text: She has decided to stay out of the program this year.

options.label: D
options.text: She has offered to partner with a newcomer this year.

explanation.summary_zh: 文中說明申請者分兩類：第一次種菜的人，以及願意與新手搭檔的資深會員。Calder 在申請開放當天就提出申請，而她從 2012 年起就租用標準菜地，不是第一次種菜的人。因此她的申請只能屬於後者，也就是今年她願意擔任新手的搭檔。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 本題要結合兩組線索。線索一在最後一段：申請者是 first-time growers 和 experienced members willing to partner with them，而 Calder submitted hers（hers 指她的申請）。這只能確定她今年有申請，可排除 C，但無法判斷她是以新手身分申請半塊菜地（A），還是以資深會員身分申請當搭檔（D）。線索二在第二段：她 has kept a standard plot since 2012，表示她不是第一次種菜的人；第一段則說半塊菜地是租給 first-time growers。這條線索單獨看，只說明她不是新手，看不出她今年是否參加。兩組線索合起來，才能確定她是以資深會員身分申請擔任搭檔，答案是 D。另外，sat out that first season 說明她去年沒有參加，可排除 B。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 她確實提出了申請，但半塊菜地是租給第一次種菜的人。她從 2012 年起就租用標準菜地，不屬於新手，所以她的申請不會是租半塊菜地。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 文中明說她 sat out that first season，也就是沒有參加方案的第一季，所以去年她沒有和新手配對。去年和 Adeyemi 配對的是 Walter Osei。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 最後一句說她在申請開放當天就提出申請，與「今年不參加」相反。去年沒參加是事實，但此選項把去年的情況錯套到今年。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。她今年提出申請，而她是資深會員、不是新手；在兩類申請者中，她只可能屬於願意與新手搭檔的資深會員。

evidence.quote: Applications from first-time growers and from experienced members willing to partner with them are due March 15 at larkspurgarden.example.
Calder submitted hers the day applications opened.
Ruth Calder, who has kept a standard plot since 2012, sat out that first season, doubting that beginners would stick with it.
Last spring, the garden began renting half plots to first-time growers
Adeyemi's partner was Walter Osei

explanation.takeaway_zh: 推論人物角色時，先確認此人做了什麼（例如提出申請），再用文中其他資訊（例如她的資歷）排除其他可能，才能判斷她的身分。也要注意時間：去年沒參加，不代表今年也不參加。

content.title: Riverside Bike Co-op Shift Schedule
content.scenario_summary: A community bicycle repair co-op posts its volunteer shift schedule for July 15–19. A table lists evening repair shifts at the garage, a maintenance class at a community center, parts shelving and a Saturday drop-in clinic. Readers are told that their names appear beside the sessions they agreed to cover. A note describes an unexpected benefit. While the garage floor was resurfaced in June, the clinic moved temporarily to a library courtyard. Organizers expected quiet weeks, but visitors kept coming for repairs and twenty-two signed up for the maintenance class. The library has invited the co-op back, so from July 19 the Saturday clinic will be held in the courtyard. Customer service will start at 10:00 A.M. instead of 9:00 A.M., and clinic volunteers will meet at the garage at 9:15 A.M. to load a tool trailer. A second note says the busy courtyard sessions used up most chain sizes, so no chain replacements may be promised until an order arrives on the morning of July 17. The questions cover four points. The first tests readership: all session volunteers, against a narrower rival (Saturday clinic staff) and groups mentioned only in the third person. The second is a chronology inference applying the chain rule to the July 15 shift. The third asks which result of the June sessions is NOT stated (new volunteers). The fourth asks for the customer opening time, contrasted with other real times in the schedule.

documents.title: Riverside Bike Co-op: Shift Schedule, July 15–19

blocks.text: Riverside Bike Co-op: Shift Schedule, July 15–19
Posted by: Lena Brooks
Your name appears next to each session you have agreed to cover. Times include setup and cleanup, so they differ from our customer hours (see riversidebike.example).
This week's sessions
Saturday Clinic Moving to the Library

While the garage floor was being resurfaced in June, we held the drop-in clinic in the courtyard of Millbrook Public Library, expecting a few quiet weeks. Instead, library visitors kept stopping by for repairs, and twenty-two of them signed up for our basic maintenance class. Pleased with the response, the library has invited us back, so from July 19 the Saturday clinic will be held in the courtyard. The garage clinic opened at 9:00 A.M., but the library allows no courtyard events before 10:00 A.M., so we will start serving customers then. Clinic volunteers should meet at the garage at 9:15 A.M. to load the tool trailer.
Chain Stock

The courtyard sessions used far more chains than expected, leaving us out of most sizes. A new order arrives on the morning of July 17. Until then, please do not promise customers a chain replacement; offer to clean and adjust their current chain instead.
If you cannot cover a session, tell Lena by noon the day before so she can find a replacement.

questions.prompt: For whom is the schedule mainly intended?

options.label: A
options.text: Customers bringing bicycles to the co-op for repairs

options.label: B
options.text: Volunteers staffing the Saturday clinic at the library

options.label: C
options.text: Volunteers covering any of the week's scheduled sessions

options.label: D
options.text: Library visitors enrolled in the maintenance class

explanation.summary_zh: 開頭的「Your name appears next to each session you have agreed to cover」是對所有排班者說的話。表格涵蓋 7 月 15 日到 19 日共五個時段，地點包括車庫、社區中心與圖書館中庭。因此本文的主要讀者是負責本週任一時段的志工，答案為 (C)。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 判斷目標讀者可分兩步：先找出文中直接以 you 稱呼的對象，再確認文件涵蓋的範圍。本文告訴讀者，名字會列在自己同意負責的時段旁；文末也請無法到場的人在前一天中午前通知 Lena。表格則同時列出車庫的晚間維修班、社區中心的課程、零件上架，以及週六免預約維修服務。週六維修服務的說明篇幅最長，但它只是五個時段之一。「Chain Stock」段落的限制只到 7 月 17 日上午到貨為止，影響的是 7 月 15 日晚班等較早的時段，與 19 日的維修服務無關。顧客與報名課程的訪客則都只以第三人稱被提及。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 顧客在文中以第三人稱出現。表格時間「differ from our customer hours」，顧客時間要另外上網查詢；文中也提醒讀者「do not promise customers a chain replacement」。可見讀者是為顧客服務的人，而不是送修的顧客本身。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 週六維修服務的志工確實屬於讀者的一部分，「Clinic volunteers should meet at the garage at 9:15 A.M.」就是給他們的指示。但表格還列出 7 月 15 日至 18 日在 Garage 與 Elm Street Community Center 的時段，圖書館中庭只用於 7 月 19 日這一場。鏈條規定也只針對 7 月 17 日上午以前的時段。此選項只涵蓋其中一場，範圍過窄。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。「each session you have agreed to cover」與「If you cannot cover a session, tell Lena」適用於表上任何時段的負責人。鏈條規定與週六集合時間則分別針對其中不同時段的志工，整份文件是寫給本週所有排班志工的。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 報名基礎保養課的 22 位圖書館訪客在文中以 them 指稱，出現在過去的敘述中，文件沒有給他們任何指示。課程那一列的 Volunteers 欄是 Sofia 與 Lena，代表負責該時段的人。開頭也說明表格時間包含布置與收拾，屬於工作人員的時段。

evidence.quote: Your name appears next to each session you have agreed to cover.
Elm Street Community Center
Clinic volunteers should meet at the garage at 9:15 A.M. to load the tool trailer.
A new order arrives on the morning of July 17. Until then, please do not promise customers a chain replacement
If you cannot cover a session, tell Lena by noon the day before so she can find a replacement.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 判斷目標讀者時，除了找出 you 被告知或被要求的事，也要比對文件涵蓋的範圍。只對應其中一部分內容的群體，以及只以第三人稱被提及的群體，都是常見的誘答。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the evening repair shift on July 15?

options.label: A
options.text: Volunteers working it should not promise customers new chains.

options.label: B
options.text: The new parts order will be shelved during it.

options.label: C
options.text: It will take place in the library courtyard.

options.label: D
options.text: Lena Brooks is scheduled to work it.

explanation.summary_zh: 鏈條新訂單要到 7 月 17 日上午才送達，在此之前不可向顧客承諾更換鏈條。7 月 15 日的晚間維修班早於到貨時間，因此該班志工不應承諾更換新鏈條，答案為 (A)。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 本題要結合兩個時間關係。第一，「Until then」的限制持續到「the morning of July 17」。第二，表格顯示這個晚班排在 July 15 傍晚。15 日早於 17 日上午，所以限制適用於這一班；相對地，7 月 18 日的晚班已在預定到貨之後。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。15 日晚班落在「Until then, please do not promise customers a chain replacement」的適用期間內，因此該班志工不應承諾更換新鏈條。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 上架零件訂單（Shelving the parts order）排在 7 月 17 日 8:30–10:30 A.M.，而訂單也是 17 日上午才到。Omar 雖然在 15 日晚班和 17 日上架時段都有排班，但上架工作不在 15 日進行。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 15 日晚班的地點是 Garage（車庫）。圖書館中庭是 7 月 19 日起週六免預約維修服務的地點，此選項把地點套到錯誤的時段。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 15 日晚班列出的志工是 Omar 與 Jun。Lena 排在 16 日的課程和 19 日的週六免預約維修服務，不在這一班。

evidence.quote: July 15
A new order arrives on the morning of July 17. Until then, please do not promise customers a chain replacement

explanation.takeaway_zh: 遇到「until／before／after＋時間」的規定時，先把題目所問事件的日期放到時間線上，看它落在界線之前還是之後，就能判斷規定是否適用。

questions.prompt: What is NOT stated about the clinic sessions held at the library in June?

options.label: A
options.text: The co-op did not expect them to be busy.

options.label: B
options.text: They brought in several new volunteer mechanics.

options.label: C
options.text: They led some visitors to enroll in a class.

options.label: D
options.text: They used more chains than the co-op had anticipated.

explanation.summary_zh: 文中提到三件事：合作社原本預期會很冷清、有訪客因此報名課程、中庭場次用掉的鏈條遠超預期。但文中沒有提到 6 月的活動帶來新的志工技師，答案為 (B)。
explanation.reasoning_zh: NOT 題要替每個選項找出對應句。「expecting a few quiet weeks」對應 A。「twenty-two of them signed up for our basic maintenance class」中的 them 指前來修車的圖書館訪客，對應 C。「Chain Stock」段落中的「The courtyard sessions」指的就是 6 月在圖書館中庭舉辦的場次，對應 D。表格雖列出多位志工的名字，但文中沒有說任何人是因 6 月的活動而新加入的。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 有提及。「expecting a few quiet weeks」表示合作社原本預期這幾週會很冷清，也就是沒料到會忙碌；下一句以 Instead 開頭，正好呼應這個落差。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確（未提及）。文中描述的結果是訪客報名課程、圖書館邀請合作社回去，以及鏈條大量消耗，沒有任何關於新志工或技師加入的敘述。表格中的 Omar、Jun 等人也沒有被說明是新成員。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 有提及。前來修車的圖書館訪客中，「twenty-two of them signed up for our basic maintenance class」，也就是有人因此報名了課程。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 有提及。「The courtyard sessions used far more chains than expected」說明 6 月中庭場次用掉的鏈條遠多於預期，導致多數尺寸缺貨。

evidence.quote: expecting a few quiet weeks
twenty-two of them signed up for our basic maintenance class
The courtyard sessions used far more chains than expected

explanation.takeaway_zh: 作答 NOT 題時，先替三個選項找到文中的明確依據，找不到依據的那一項就是答案。不要因為某個結果聽起來合理，就以為文中有寫；也要留意不同段落可能用不同說法指同一件事。

questions.prompt: What time will the July 19 clinic open to customers?

explanation.summary_zh: 文中說明圖書館不允許在 10:00 A.M. 之前於中庭舉辦活動，「so we will start serving customers then」。因此 7 月 19 日的維修服務從 10:00 開始接待顧客，答案為 (D)。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 題目問的是「對顧客開放」的時間。表格中 7 月 19 日那一列的 9:15 A.M. 是志工時段的起點，而開頭已說明表格時間包含布置與收拾，與顧客時間不同；9:15 是志工到車庫集合、裝載工具拖車的時間。9:00 則是過去在車庫舉辦時的開始時間。真正的對外開放時間是說明段落中的 10:00。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 8:30 A.M. 是 7 月 17 日在車庫上架零件訂單的開始時間，屬於另一項工作，與週六免預約維修服務無關。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 9:00 A.M. 是維修服務在車庫舉辦時的開始時間（The garage clinic opened at 9:00 A.M.）。改到圖書館中庭後，這個時間已不再適用。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 9:15 A.M. 是志工在車庫集合、裝載工具拖車的時間，也是表格中志工時段的起點。依開頭說明，表格時間與顧客時間不同。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。圖書館在 10:00 A.M. 前不允許舉辦中庭活動，因此合作社從 10:00 開始服務顧客。

evidence.quote: The garage clinic opened at 9:00 A.M., but the library allows no courtyard events before 10:00 A.M., so we will start serving customers then.
Clinic volunteers should meet at the garage at 9:15 A.M. to load the tool trailer.
Times include setup and cleanup, so they differ from our customer hours

explanation.takeaway_zh: 作答時間題時，先確認題目問的是哪一個事件、對哪一群人而言。同一場活動可能同時有工作人員的集合時間和對外開放時間。

content.title: Newcomer Award Video Trial at the Harlow County Business Council
content.scenario_summary: In January, a county business council posts a notice launching a trial. Newcomer Award entrants may submit a three-minute video instead of a written statement. After the May awards dinner, the chair of the awards committee will discuss the results with the judges and recommend to the executive director whether other categories should accept videos. Gavin Pryce of the council staff checks each video's length and sound and contacts entrants about problems, and Tessa Grant, also of the staff, e-mails entrants to confirm receipt. Phone help with recording or uploading comes from the office administrator, and the events coordinator sells dinner tickets. After the dinner, Helen Ferreira e-mails Paul Okonjo. She recommends video entries in all six categories next year under the trial's procedures. Entrants uploaded through the website because the council's e-mail system rejected most sample files for size in a December staff test. Home viewing for judges was an unplanned benefit. Separately, the deadline was set two weeks later than usual because owners expected filming to take longer than writing. Sanjay Mehta took all fourteen upload-help calls. In July, Gavin moves to sponsorship and Tessa to membership; Lina Marsh takes over all of Gavin's awards work and Omar Haddad all of Tessa's. At the March members' breakfast, owners said they would hesitate to submit videos for other categories, assuming the judges would favor professional filming. In one sentence, Helen notes that Ama Okafor personally recorded a simple tour of her bakery on a borrowed phone as her Newcomer entry; in a separate sentence, she reports that the bakery later won the Newcomer Award at the awards dinner. She then suggests inviting Ama to speak to prospective entrants, without stating the invitation's purpose. The questions cover five points. The first traces the problem-contact duty from Gavin to Lina; from the e-mail alone, Omar, Tessa's successor, is an equally plausible rival. The second separates the website reason from the deadline's stated reason and a side effect. The third identifies the e-mail's main purpose among true subordinate content. The fourth infers Helen's role by matching the notice's chair-to-director recommendation flow with the e-mail's sender, recipient and content. The fifth infers the motive for inviting the winner by combining across sentences the owners' concern, Ama's personal borrowed-phone recording and the separately reported later award, with rivals that link Okafor to an upload demonstration, the owners' assumed judging preference for professional filming treated as fact, or a new judging preference for phone-recorded entries.

documents.title: Newcomer Award: Video Entries Accepted This Year

blocks.text: Harlow County Business Council
Newcomer Award: Video Entries Accepted This Year
Posted: January 6

This year, Newcomer Award entrants may submit a video of up to three minutes instead of the usual written statement. This is a trial. After the awards dinner, the chair of the awards committee will discuss the results with the judges and recommend to the executive director whether videos should be offered in other categories.

Upload videos at harlowbusiness.example by February 28. Before judging, staff member Gavin Pryce will confirm each video runs no longer than three minutes and has clear sound. If not, he will contact you for a corrected version. Staff member Tessa Grant will e-mail you to confirm receipt.
For recording or upload help, call the office administrator at 555-0186. The events coordinator sells May 15 awards dinner tickets.
From: Helen Ferreira
To: Paul Okonjo
Date: May 19
Subject: Video trial: my recommendation
Dear Paul,

Now that the awards dinner is behind us, here is my recommendation: next year, the council should accept video entries in all six categories. The Newcomer judges told me the videos showed owners' premises, staff and products better than written statements could. Newcomer entries also rose from eleven last year to nineteen.

I would keep the trial's procedures for every category. We had planned to accept videos by e-mail, but when staff e-mailed sample files to one another in December, the council's e-mail system rejected most of them because of their size. We therefore had entrants upload through the website instead. As it turned out, this also let the judges watch entries at home, which several said they valued. The deadline was set two weeks later than usual because owners at our autumn workshop expected filming to take longer than writing. Sanjay Mehta took all fourteen calls from entrants who needed upload help, and every video arrived on time.
In July, Gavin Pryce moves to sponsorship and Tessa Grant to membership. Lina Marsh will take over all Gavin's awards work and Omar Haddad all Tessa's. Both should be briefed before entries open.

At the March members' breakfast, several owners said they would hesitate to submit videos for other categories, assuming the judges would favor professionally filmed entries. For her Newcomer entry, Ama Okafor recorded a simple tour of her bakery herself, using a borrowed phone. At the awards dinner, her bakery won the Newcomer Award. I suggest inviting her to speak at our September information session for prospective entrants.
Best regards, Helen

questions.prompt: If Ms. Ferreira's recommendation is adopted, who will most likely contact next year's entrants whose videos run longer than three minutes?

explanation.summary_zh: 公告指出，影片送交評審前，由 Gavin Pryce 確認長度不超過三分鐘（剛好三分鐘也符合），且音質清楚。不符合時，他會聯絡參賽者，請對方提交修正版本。Tessa Grant 則負責寄電子郵件確認收件。郵件中，Helen 建議所有類別沿用試辦程序，並說明七月起 Gavin 的獎項工作全數由 Lina Marsh 接手，Tessa 的工作則由 Omar Haddad 接手。因此，若建議被採納，明年聯絡影片超過三分鐘之參賽者的人最可能是 Lina。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 第一步，從公告分辨兩位工作人員原本的職責。Gavin 在評審前確認每支影片 no longer than three minutes（三分鐘以內，含三分鐘）且音質清楚；If not（不符合）時，他會聯絡參賽者索取修正版本。超過三分鐘的影片就屬於這種情況。Tessa 則負責寄信確認收件。第二步，看郵件。Helen 建議 keep the trial's procedures for every category，所以若建議被採納，這套檢查與聯絡程序會延續到明年。七月起，Gavin 轉往 sponsorship，Tessa 轉往 membership；Lina 接手 all Gavin's awards work，Omar 接手 Tessa 的工作，兩人都要在報名開放前接受說明。郵件沒有寫出 Gavin 與 Tessa 各自負責什麼，所以只讀郵件時，Lina 與 Omar 都可能是答案。只讀公告，則只能找到交接前的負責人 Gavin。結合兩份文件來看：聯絡影片不符規定的參賽者是 Gavin 的工作，而他的獎項工作由 Lina 接手。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公告中負責檢查影片並聯絡不符規定參賽者的確實是 Gavin，但這是今年試辦期間的安排。郵件指出，他七月轉往 sponsorship，獎項工作全數交給 Lina。題目問的是明年，選 A 等於把交接前的負責人當成交接後的負責人。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公告說錄製或上傳的協助由行政專員以電話提供；郵件說 Sanjay 接聽了所有尋求上傳協助的來電。這是回應參賽者求助的工作，兩份文件都沒有把檢查影片長度或聯絡不符規定參賽者的工作交給他，郵件的交接說明也沒有提到他。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。根據公告，影片超過三分鐘時，聯絡參賽者索取修正版本是 Gavin 的工作。郵件指出 Lina 將接手 Gavin 全部的獎項工作；若建議被採納、試辦程序沿用，檢查影片並聯絡不符規定參賽者的工作便會由 Lina 負責。因此，明年最可能由 Lina 聯絡影片超時的參賽者。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: Omar 同樣是明年獎項工作的承接者，但他接手的是 Tessa 的工作。公告中 Tessa 負責寄電子郵件確認收件，這雖然也算與參賽者聯絡，卻不是在影片不符規定時聯絡參賽者。後者屬於 Gavin 的工作，由 Lina 接手。

evidence.quote: Before judging, staff member Gavin Pryce will confirm each video runs no longer than three minutes and has clear sound. If not, he will contact you for a corrected version. Staff member Tessa Grant will e-mail you to confirm receipt.
I would keep the trial's procedures for every category.
In July, Gavin Pryce moves to sponsorship and Tessa Grant to membership. Lina Marsh will take over all Gavin's awards work and Omar Haddad all Tessa's. Both should be briefed before entries open.
For recording or upload help, call the office administrator at 555-0186.
Sanjay Mehta took all fourteen calls from entrants who needed upload help

explanation.takeaway_zh: 職責交接題可分兩步作答。先在一份文件確認目標工作原本由誰負責，再到另一份文件找出此人的工作交給了誰。若有多位承接者，要看各自接手的是哪一位原負責人的工作。也要確認題目問的時間點在交接之前還是之後。

questions.prompt: According to the e-mail, why did the council have entrants upload their videos through its website?

options.label: A
options.text: Judges wanted to be able to watch entries at home.

options.label: B
options.text: Staff found most test videos were too big to e-mail.

options.label: C
options.text: Owners expected filming to take longer than writing.

options.label: D
options.text: Staff had to check each video's length before judging.

explanation.summary_zh: 郵件說，議會原本打算用電子郵件收件。但十二月工作人員互寄樣本影片時，議會的電子郵件系統因檔案太大，拒收了大部分影片。下一句用 therefore 說明，因此改請參賽者從網站上傳。B「工作人員發現大部分測試影片太大，無法用電子郵件寄送」正是這個原因的改寫。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 這段同時出現兩組因果和一個附帶結果，要先分清楚各自對應哪個決定。①系統因檔案大小拒收影片，therefore 改用網站上傳，這是本題要找的原因。②截止日比往年晚兩週，because 業主預期拍攝比寫書面說明花時間，這是另一個決定的原因。③As it turned out, this also... 引出改用網站後才出現的附帶好處：評審可以在家觀看。題目問的是「改用網站上傳」的原因，所以只有①符合。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 評審能在家觀看，是由 As it turned out（結果發現）和 also 引出的附帶好處；several said they valued 是評審事後的評價。文中沒有說評審事先提出這項要求，所以這是決定帶來的結果，不是原因。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。原文 rejected most of them because of their size 改寫為 too big to e-mail；staff e-mailed sample files to one another 就是工作人員所做的測試。下一句的 therefore 把這件事連到改用網站上傳的決定。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 郵件確實用 because 明確提出這個理由，但它解釋的是「截止日比往年晚兩週」，不是改用網站上傳。這是把真實的理由配到錯誤的決定上。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公告確實寫明影片送交評審前由 Gavin 確認長度，但兩份文件都沒有把長度檢查說成改用網站上傳的原因。這是真實的程序配上錯誤的因果關係。

evidence.quote: when staff e-mailed sample files to one another in December, the council's e-mail system rejected most of them because of their size. We therefore had entrants upload through the website instead.
As it turned out, this also let the judges watch entries at home, which several said they valued.
The deadline was set two weeks later than usual because owners at our autumn workshop expected filming to take longer than writing.
Before judging, staff member Gavin Pryce will confirm each video runs no longer than three minutes and has clear sound.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 一段文字中若有好幾個 because、therefore 等因果標記，要先確認每個原因對應的是哪一個決定，再核對題目問的是哪一個決定。在「this also let the judges…」中，決定（改用網站）讓評審得以在家觀看，屬於決定帶來的效果；As it turned out 表示事後才發現。also 只表示『另外』，本身不代表效果。判斷因果時，要看 because、therefore、let 等連接方式或結構所表示的方向。

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the e-mail?

options.label: A
options.text: To recommend extending video entries to all categories

options.label: B
options.text: To suggest a speaker for an upcoming information session

options.label: C
options.text: To report that a staff member's duties will change

options.label: D
options.text: To share this year's entry figures for the Newcomer Award

explanation.summary_zh: 主旨行寫著 my recommendation，第一段開頭也直接提出建議：明年六個類別都接受影片參賽。A「把影片參賽擴大到所有類別」正是整封信的核心目的。
explanation.reasoning_zh: Helen 開頭先提出建議，再以評審的評價和報名數增加作為支持。後面談到的沿用試辦程序、上傳與截止日的安排、人員交接和邀請講者，都是推行這項建議時的說明或補充構想。判斷主旨時，要區分寫信的核心目的與信中真實但次要的內容。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。主旨行和首段都表明，這封信是在試辦結束後提出建議：明年所有類別都接受影片參賽。extending video entries to all categories 改寫了 accept video entries in all six categories。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: 最後一段確實建議邀請 Ama Okafor 在九月說明會演講，但這是附帶的推廣構想，不是整封信的主要目的。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: Gavin 與 Tessa 七月轉調、分別由 Lina 與 Omar 接手確有其事。但信中提到這點，是為了讓沿用程序時能在報名開放前向 Lina 與 Omar 兩人說明（Both should be briefed before entries open），屬於配合主要建議的次要內容。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 新秀獎報名數從去年 11 件增加到 19 件，是用來支持建議的證據之一，不是寫信的目的。

evidence.quote: Subject: Video trial: my recommendation
here is my recommendation: next year, the council should accept video entries in all six categories.

explanation.takeaway_zh: 主旨題可先看主旨行與開頭，再判斷後文的數據、人事安排或附帶建議是否在支持這個核心訊息。真實但次要的內容常被拿來當作干擾選項。

questions.prompt: What position does Ms. Ferreira most likely hold?

options.label: D
options.text: The chair of the awards committee

explanation.summary_zh: 公告說明，頒獎晚宴後由獎項委員會主席與評審討論結果，並向執行長建議其他類別是否應開放影片參賽。郵件中，Helen 在晚宴結束後寫信給 Paul，提出的正是這項建議：明年六個類別都接受影片。因此 Helen 最可能是獎項委員會主席。
explanation.reasoning_zh: 公告只說明「主席向執行長提出建議」，沒有寫出主席或執行長是誰。郵件寫出了寄件人、收件人和建議內容，卻沒有寫任何人的職稱，只看郵件無法確定 Helen 的職位。把兩者對起來：發出這項建議的是主席，接收建議的是執行長。Helen 是寄件人，所以她對應主席，收件人 Paul 則對應執行長。

option_analysis.label: A
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公告中的執行長是「接收」建議的一方。Helen 是寄出建議的人，收件人是 Paul，所以執行長對應的是 Paul，而不是 Helen。

option_analysis.label: B
option_analysis.reason_zh: Helen 雖然提到晚宴已結束，也提到九月說明會，但公告交給活動協調人員的只有 5 月 15 日晚宴的票務。負責在晚宴後提出影片建議的是獎項委員會主席。

option_analysis.label: C
option_analysis.reason_zh: 公告指定由行政專員以電話協助錄製與上傳。郵件則說尋求上傳協助的來電都是 Sanjay 接的，所以行政專員最可能是 Sanjay。此外，提出建議也不是公告交給行政專員的工作。

option_analysis.label: D
option_analysis.reason_zh: 正確。公告指出，晚宴後由獎項委員會主席與評審討論並向執行長提出建議。Helen 正是在晚宴後寄出這項建議，也提到評審告訴她的意見，與主席的職責相符。

evidence.quote: After the awards dinner, the chair of the awards committee will discuss the results with the judges and recommend to the executive director whether videos should be offered in other categories.
From: Helen Ferreira
To: Paul Okonjo
Now that the awards dinner is behind us, here is my recommendation: next year, the council should accept video entries in all six categories.
For recording or upload help, call the office administrator at 555-0186. The events coordinator sells May 15 awards dinner tickets.
Sanjay Mehta took all fourteen calls from entrants who needed upload help

explanation.takeaway_zh: 推斷職位時，可把一份文件中「誰向誰做某事」的職責流程，對到另一份文件的寄件人、收件人與內容。要分清楚發出方與接收方，不要只憑職稱聽起來像不像來判斷。

questions.prompt: Why does Ms. Ferreira most likely suggest inviting Ms. Okafor to the September session?

options.label: A
options.text: To demonstrate how to upload a video recorded on a phone

options.label: B
options.text: To explain why the judges favored professionally filmed entries

options.label: C
options.text: To show that a winning video need not be professionally filmed

options.label: D
